PullRequest.Title: Agent host: index sent requests and answer request searches (proposed by opus 5.5)
PullRequest.Body:

Proposed implementation for #349148.

Part 1 of 3 for searching the requests you've sent to Agent Host sessions across all connected hosts. This PR adds the host side. The link reveal is #349135, and the client search UI and tool are #349136, stacked on this PR.

## What changes

Each agent host now indexes the requests users send to its sessions. It answers a new VS Code extension request, `vscode/searchRequests`, so clients can find a request without restoring or pinning any session.

- **Results.** A search returns up to 50 hits, newest first. Each hit has:
  - the session and chat URIs
  - the turn ID the host currently exposes, so a link's `turn=` still resolves after the chat is restored
  - the start time and the session and chat titles
  - a snippet of about 200 characters around the first match
- **Result metadata.** Each result reports whether indexing is on, the time of the oldest request the index still holds (`indexedSince`), and whether more matches exist beyond the limit.
- **Capability.** Hosts advertise the `vscode.searchRequests` capability in their initialize meta. Clients only query hosts that advertise it, so older hosts are reported as unsupported instead of failing.
- **Setting.** The new setting `chat.agentHost.requestSearch.enabled` is on by default, marked preview, and mirrored to the host. Turning it off stops indexing and deletes the index.

Example result:

```json
{ "indexEnabled": true, "truncated": false, "indexedSince": "2025-11-17T09:00:00.000Z",
  "hits": [{ "session": "copilot:/abc", "chat": "copilot:/abc#peer", "turnId": "9f2…", "startedAt": "2025-11-18T10:23:00.000Z",
             "sessionTitle": "Schema migration", "chatTitle": "Rollback plan", "snippet": "…please migrate the schema to…" }] }
```

## How it changes

- **`AgentHostRequestIndex`** (node) keeps its own SQLite file, `request-index.db`, next to the host config. Keeping it out of `agent-host.db` means it needs no cross-build migration.
  - Search is a plain table queried with `instr` over a lowercased copy of the text. Every term must match, terms match substrings, and one- and two-character terms work.
  - Each request is capped at 10k characters and the index at 20k rows.
- **`RequestIndexContribution`** is a chat lifecycle contribution:
  - It records visible user-origin request text when a turn starts.
  - It prunes the index on client-initiated truncation and on chat deletion. Moved chats keep their entries, distinguished by `chatRemovalReason`.
  - It follows chat moves and title changes.
  - It skips subagent sessions, ephemeral sessions and relay lanes. Deleted and hidden sessions are filtered out at query time.
- **Turn IDs.** A hit uses the live turn ID when the chat currently holds it. Otherwise it uses the provider's restored ID from the session database's event-ID mapping.
- **Protocol.** `searchRequests` is added to `IAgentService` and `IAgentConnection`.
  - The `ProtocolServerHandler` handler accepts direct transports only and validates parameters.
  - `AgentHostProtocolClient` checks the capability and validates the result.
  - The local and editor-remote services delegate to it.
- **Docs.** `src/vs/platform/agentHost/AGENTS.md` §3e documents the index.

## Design decisions

- **Rejected: querying the Copilot SDK's `session-store.db`.** It covers Copilot sessions only, its schema is owned by the SDK, and the SDK has no RPC to query it.
- **Rejected: scanning transcripts** through `get_session_context` or the saved-chat readers. These restore and pin each session, which is too heavy for searching many sessions.
- **Rejected: adding tables to `agent-host.db`.** That would require cross-build migrations.
- **Not indexed:**
  - responses and steering messages
  - requests sent before the index existed (there is no backfill; `indexedSince` makes this visible)
- **Extension method, not a standard command.** This uses a VS Code extension method rather than a standard AHP command. A standard search command could be proposed upstream later.

## How to test

Send a few requests in Agent Host sessions, then search for them with the client in #349136. Without the client, you can send `vscode/searchRequests` over the protocol.

Targeted tests (all passing):
- `node node_modules/mocha/bin/mocha.js test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --exit --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostRequestIndex.test.ts` — 7 passing. They cover:
  - search ordering and titles
  - restored turn IDs
  - suppressed sessions and truncation
  - moved and deleted chats
  - the off switch deleting the index
  - snippets
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\protocol\requestSearch.integrationTest.ts` — passing. It starts a real agent host process with the mock agent, sends turns over WebSocket and searches them over the wire.
- The agent host node test suite, including the new `protocolServerHandler` tests, passed: 1204 tests.
- The electron `agentHostProtocolClient` test passed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The OFFSET loop, post-query suppression, retained deleted-session rows and index definitions directly establish repeated prefix evaluation. The number of suppressed matching requests and actual duration are workload-dependent, not uncertainties in the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Repeated SQLite row visits, substring predicate evaluation and database-page reads.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: With M matching rows skipped because their sessions are suppressed and page size P = limit + 1, SQL examines prefixes of P, 2P, 3P, etc., producing approximately O(M²/P) qualifying-row visits rather than O(M). Thousands of retained requests from a deleted default chat suffice; the index permits roughly 20,000 retained rows. Suppression checks remain once per distinct session, not once per row.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Superlinear CPU and database-read work increases search latency and holds the shared index Sequencer, delaying subsequent searches and queued indexing work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: There was no request-index pagination or repeated substring-query work before this PR. The new search introduces repeated prefix scans, beyond the single bounded table traversal needed for its chosen substring-search semantics.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new search pages matching requests with an increasing OFFSET, then filters suppressed sessions outside SQLite. Each additional page reevaluates the substring predicates over the already-skipped prefix.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added loop at lines 177-180 reruns WHERE instr(folded, ...) ORDER BY started_at DESC, seq DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ? with offset incremented by each page's length. Lines 184-190 skip suppressed sessions without advancing a SQL key cursor or removing their rows.
Findings.Title: Use cursor pagination when skipping suppressed requests
Findings.Impact: A common-term search after deleting or hiding a long chat can execute hundreds of increasingly expensive page queries even when it ultimately returns no hits. Warm caches do not remove the repeated substring evaluation.
Findings.Evidence: The only relevant SQL indexes are requests_by_time and requests_by_chat; neither indexes instr predicates. OFFSET must find and skip preceding qualifying rows again on every statement. Suppression is cached once per distinct session, but this does not cache the SQL prefix scan. Deleted sessions can leave large matching prefixes: RequestIndexContribution removes rows for SessionChatRemoved only, whereas AgentHostStateManager.deleteSession calls removeSession and emits root/sessionRemoved/onDidDeleteSession, not per-chat removal actions (node/agentHostStateManager.ts:2399-2488). The new test also explicitly retains indexed requests while suppressing their session.
Findings.Recommendation: Page by the last visited (started_at, seq) tuple instead of OFFSET, retaining the existing ordering and suppression filtering so each candidate row is visited only once per search.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The serial per-row call chain, unconditional stat, immediate last-reference eviction and connection initialization are directly established by the implementation. The trigger explicitly uses cold, otherwise-unheld databases; only the storage-dependent duration is unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem existence probes, SQLite connection opens/closes, journal-configuration statements and schema-version checks.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For H cold hits across G storage resources, the implementation performs H stats and, when no other owner holds the databases, H connection initializations rather than G. H defaults to 20 and can reach 50, including 20 or 50 hits from one chat. Truncation can invoke the same helper for hundreds of candidate turns. Operations are awaited serially inside the index-wide Sequencer.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Additional serial filesystem/database I/O delays search results and subsequent searches and index operations queued behind them.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, the host had no request-search path performing these storage probes and database opens. The new implementation adds repeated initialization even when multiple hits share one storage resource.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new search resolves each nonresident hit's turn ID by separately acquiring and immediately disposing its session-database reference. Truncation uses the same helper for each candidate turn.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added _eventId calls tryOpenDatabase at line 247 and disposes its reference at line 254. search awaits _toHit per returned row, which reaches _exposedTurnId/_eventId for cold chats; truncateChat also awaits _eventId inside its row loop.
Findings.Title: Reuse database references across turn-ID lookups
Findings.Impact: After restarting the host, searching for a term occurring repeatedly in one historical chat can reopen the same session.db 20 times for the default result limit, or 50 times at the maximum. Repeating the search repeats the opens despite warm OS caches; slow or redirected user-data storage magnifies the latency.
Findings.Evidence: SessionDataService.tryOpenDatabase (node/sessionDataService.ts:132-146) performs a filesystem stat on every call. Its ReferenceCollection destroys the object as soon as the last reference is disposed (base/common/lifecycle.ts:704-708), and SessionDatabaseCollection destroys it by calling dispose. Thus, for an unheld cold database, successive hits each create a fresh SessionDatabase. SessionDatabase._ensureDb (node/sessionDatabase.ts:684-703) repeats mkdir, SQLite open, journal configuration and migration-version checks before getTurnEventId. There is no operation-scoped reference reuse in this index.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep an operation-scoped map of storage resources to database references (including missing-database results), reuse each reference for all mappings in that search or truncation, and dispose the references in a finally block after the operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Host startup, recording new requests, and updating request titles
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Constructing AgentService and registering the contribution construct the index service but do not open its SQLite database. A turn-start hook captures metadata and queues recording without awaiting it; database work is off the provider-turn critical path. A later search waits behind queued writes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dynamically load SQLite, open request-index.db, inspect filesystem locality and configure its journal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialization on first queued write or search per enabled database lifetime; the database promise is subsequently reused. No initialization per request after a successful open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No request-index file, connection, filesystem-locality check or initialization existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous initialization blocks the index queue, not synchronous turn dispatch; it blocks a first search that needs it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Insert the turn, upsert available session/chat titles, and periodically prune request rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request insert and up to two title writes per recorded turn; one pruning statement every 100 recordings. Searchable text is capped at 10,000 characters, with a folded copy. Request rows are pruned to approximately 20,000; titles are maintained separately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No request-index writes or pruning were performed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs serially in the index-wide Sequencer, outside turn dispatch; searches wait for earlier queued writes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Eligible turn starts and title changes; subagent and ephemeral sessions are excluded. Nonsearchable turns retain ordering metadata but not request text.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One global Sequencer serializes index reads, writes and close/delete operations. Contribution dispatch does not await queued writes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The request-index connection is lazy and reused after opening; an opening failure is memoized until close. Titles are persisted rather than cached per operation. Disabling the setting prevents new writes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: lazy _open, fire-and-forget _write and the contribution registration/call chain are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual recording rate, text lengths, title-history size and local-versus-network storage are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate startup or normal-recording regression reported: initialization is lazy and database writes are off the turn critical path. Reviewed caps, title retention, queue ownership and journal behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search requests whose original turn IDs remain resident
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The client capability check precedes a single extension request. The server validates the query, delegates to the index and awaits its queue, SQL matching, suppression checks and hit construction before returning results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send vscode/searchRequests and return its result over the existing direct transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request/response per invocation on a supported host. Unsupported clients fail before sending; relay clients do not receive the capability or reach the index.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The request-search extension method and its transport messages did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The caller awaits the complete response, including index work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize query/results and validate result objects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Query length is at most 200 characters and eight deduplicated terms. Server results contain at most 50 hits, normally 20, with snippets of at most 202 characters plus metadata. No transcript serialization is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No request-search payload was serialized or validated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Request/result transport and validation are on the search critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the substring index, check suppression, obtain fallback titles and read the oldest retained user-request time.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: With no suppressed matches, one result-page query; one suppression SELECT per distinct session in the visited candidates; zero to two fallback-title SELECTs per returned hit; one oldest-time query. A low-selectivity or absent term can scan the bounded request table.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No request-search queries or suppression/title reads for this feature occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All are awaited before returning hits. Resident original IDs avoid session-database mapping entirely.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Roughly 20,000 retained requests, up to 10,000 characters each, eight terms, and at most 50 returned hits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entire searches share the index-wide Sequencer. Hit construction and suppression checks are serial, not Promise.all fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm request-index connection is reused. Suppression is cached by session only within the search. Resident state supplies titles and original turn IDs where available; there is no query-result cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: protocol delegation, parameter bounds, resident-ID shortcut and SQL call counts are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Request sizes, term selectivity and storage latency determine actual response duration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for the intentional bounded substring scan or result serialization. Cold-ID mapping and suppressed-match pagination introduce distinct avoidable costs covered by the findings.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search historical requests after host restart or chat eviction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each returned cold hit awaits its exposed turn-ID mapping before the result can be sent. Multiple hits are processed sequentially inside the index queue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat session.db and, on each otherwise-unheld acquisition, perform mkdir, open SQLite and inspect filesystem locality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: H stat calls for H cold mapped hits; H real connection initializations when no other owner holds those databases, even for H hits sharing one storage URI. H defaults to 20 and is capped at 50, rather than being reduced to G distinct storage resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Request search did not perform these probes or opens.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serially awaited during hit construction; delays this search and subsequent queued index operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Configure each fresh connection, check migration version, select the event-ID mapping and close the connection on last-reference disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mapping SELECT per cold hit is required by the implementation, but connection initialization is also repeated per hit because references are released immediately. No migrations need be pending for journal/version work to repeat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-hit connection setup for request search existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection initialization and mapping are on the result critical path. Close is initiated by disposal, which immediately evicts the ref-counted object.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H cold hits across G storage resources, especially a common term producing 20 or 50 hits from one historical chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One index operation at a time; per-hit mapping and initialization are serial. This is repeated work, not an uncontrolled concurrent-open burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SessionDataService shares connections only while references coexist. Immediate disposal removes the last reference, so repeated hits and subsequent searches do not retain this connection cache. Warm OS pages do not eliminate stat, reopen or initialization. Missing databases are also probed repeatedly.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the per-hit helper, unconditional stat, ReferenceCollection destruction and lazy connection initialization are all traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual milliseconds depend on storage and whether another subsystem temporarily holds a reference; the cold, unheld scenario is sufficient to establish the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported repeated session-database acquisition/initialization. An operation-scoped reference map bounds setup by distinct storage resource without caching authoritative turn state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search after deleting or hiding chats' owning sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The search must page through suppressed matching requests before it can return enough visible hits or determine there are none. Each page finishes before the next page starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rerun the substring query with increasing OFFSET and check owning-session suppression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For M suppressed matching rows and P = limit + 1, approximately M/P result-page statements repeatedly scan qualifying prefixes, giving O(M²/P) qualifying-row visits. Suppression SELECTs are correctly cached once per distinct session, and suppressed rows never reach session-database ID mapping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No request-search pagination or repeated prefix evaluation existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Repeated scans block this search and occupy the shared index Sequencer until enough visible hits are found or matches end.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Thousands of matching retained requests in deleted or hidden sessions, potentially most of the roughly 20,000-row index. Permanent session deletion does not dispatch the per-chat removal action handled by the contribution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The query-page loop, suppression lookups and all other index operations are globally serialized. No per-row subprocesses or external network requests occur.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The connection and OS pages can be warm, and the per-search suppression map prevents duplicate host-database checks. Neither caches the instr predicate evaluation or OFFSET prefix traversal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: OFFSET progression, post-query suppression, indexes and session-deletion notification behavior establish the quadratic-prefix mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of retained suppressed matches and average request text size are unknown; both control magnitude rather than mechanism validity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported OFFSET-driven repeated work. Keyset pagination using the existing time/sequence ordering preserves behavior while avoiding prefix rescans.

Scenarios.Scenario: Client truncation, chat removal/move and renaming
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Contribution hooks enqueue index maintenance without awaiting it, so index maintenance does not directly block the provider operation. Searches and other index work arriving afterward wait for the maintenance to finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read candidate turn positions, delete truncated/removed request rows, update ownership or upsert a title.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Clear-all truncation is one DELETE. Point truncation reads K indexed turns for that chat and examines candidates newest-first. Removal is two DELETEs; move and title change are one UPDATE/upsert each.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These lifecycle actions did not maintain a request index.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initiating action's synchronous critical path, but occupies the index queue before following searches.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe and acquire the chat's session database while comparing restored event IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One _eventId call per examined candidate whose original ID does not equal the kept ID, potentially hundreds of candidates from the same chat. Each call stats the file; otherwise-unheld connections are reopened. Existing active-owner references can avoid opens but not stats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Truncation had no additional request-index mapping loop or its storage probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serially awaited within truncation's index task and delays subsequent searches; not awaited by the contribution caller.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K retained turns in the affected chat and distance from the newest indexed turn to the kept turn; the retained request-table cap bounds K.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All maintenance runs through the same global Sequencer. Per-candidate ID mapping is awaited serially; moves/removals do not spawn concurrent boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No operation-scoped mapping-reference or negative-result reuse. Existing turn/session databases are reused only while another owner holds them. Server-origin truncations are correctly excluded from index truncation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: action-origin gating, SQL operations and per-row helper calls are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical truncation depth and concurrent database ownership are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: The per-candidate database-lifecycle cost is included in the shared reference-reuse finding, not duplicated. No separate performance regression found in moves, normal removals or renaming.

Scenarios.Scenario: Disable request search and dispose the host index
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration hook queues close/delete after earlier index operations; callers do not synchronously await it. Disabled searches return an empty disabled result without opening the database. Disposal queues close and prevents subsequent opens.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Close the existing request-index connection after queued work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One close for an existing connection; subsequent queued closes encounter no connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after the index queue drains and outside turn dispatch; earlier long searches can delay cleanup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove the database and WAL/SHM/rollback-journal sidecars.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four concurrent force-removal calls per queued deletion for a file-backed index; none for an in-memory index. While disabled, further root-config change notifications can queue another deletion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No request-index files or associated removal operations existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous configuration cleanup, not blocking chat progress. Subsequent enabled index work is ordered behind it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configuration-change frequency and the lifetime of the index; deletion cardinality is constant per notification.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Queue ordering serializes close/delete with index tasks; only the four sidecar-removal calls use Promise.all.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Close clears the cached database promise. Re-enabling creates a fresh index lazily. Disabled writes are rejected before opening or queueing database work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: configuration listener, disabled guards and serialized cleanup are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configuration changes are low-frequency; cleanup duration depends on prior queued work and storage.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate high-confidence performance regression: cleanup ownership is explicit and boundary cardinality is constant. Earlier reported search costs can delay cleanup but are not duplicated as lifecycle findings.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 27 changed files and all diff pages against base bfbaab8611c6df0f12d176833f08091ee22a5bb0. Reported two introduced medium-severity regressions: repeated cold session-database initialization during ID mapping and quadratic OFFSET prefix rescans for suppressed matches. Accounted for critical paths, boundary counts, resident/cold and positive/negative cache behavior, sequencing, lifecycle cleanup and payload/retention bounds. No concrete pre-existing performance regression fix was identified. Conclusions are based on static call-path and ownership evidence; storage-dependent durations were not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
